name: 619-batchdecode-tinyllama-1gpu
model: TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0. Ungated; ~2.2 GB of bf16 weights, already in the local HF cache.
hardware: 1x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3, one node, one GPU.
parallelism: tp1. No tensor, pipeline, expert or data parallelism.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=64, warmup the first 25%, bounded at 3000 requests with an 1800 s safety cap.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no shared prefix: prompts centred on 512 tokens (stdev 64, clamped 384-640) and generations centred on 512 tokens (stdev 32, clamped 448-576), sent to /v1/completions rather than the chat route, seed 42.
purpose: A compact chat assistant drafting half-page replies for 64 concurrent users from medium-length prompts on one GPU.
launch:
# sglang at commit 5d264a90ac5154d8e368ee558337dd3dd92e720b (`git describe --tags` = v0.1.20).
# Flat `key: value` only: an indented block is DROPPED by the engine's line reader and the
# server then starts without the mechanism this file declares.
# The flashinfer attention path is ON (the engine default) and is the declared operating point.
# `--disable-flashinfer` is NOT a substitute for the key below: it swaps the attention kernels
# as well, and turns graph capture off silently on top of that.

model-path: TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0
tp-size: 1

# LAUNCH HAZARD, not a preference. With graph replay on, this engine stops making progress the
# first time the resident batch is not one of the sizes it captured ([1, 2, 4], then multiples
# of 8 up to 120): the padded rows are given a zero-length sequence and the decode never comes
# back -- no error, no traceback, no exit, the server log simply ends mid-run. A closed loop
# leaves the captured sizes the moment one request finishes, so this is unavoidable here.
disable-cuda-graph: true

# ~65 GB of KV pool, ~2.9M tokens. Pinned rather than left to __post_init__, which picks 0.88.
mem-fraction-static: 0.85

# One SSE chunk per token. The dataclass default at this commit is 8, which would make
# guidellm's `inter_token_latency_ms` a chunk cadence rather than a token cadence.
stream-interval: 1

random-seed: 42

# host / port are supplied at launch; context-length comes from the checkpoint (2048).
